title: Qwen vs the computer inside its own weights
black: mcu-max chess engine (depth 2, ≤1000 nodes) running on the RISC-V CPU compiled into Qwen's own weights
about: Every engine move is computed by the RV32IM CPU that lives in Qwenputer's extra layers (its RAM is the model's Gated DeltaNet state). Instruction counts are exact for finished moves; the in-progress count is an estimate from tokens.

plies.qwen_text: The position is the standard opening setup with pawns on the second rank. I need to make a move to start developing my pieces and controlling the center. A common and solid opening move is to play e4, which claims central space and opens lines for my queen and bishop.

Black has responded with the Sicilian Defense (c5), a solid and popular opening that challenges my center. I have a pawn on e4 and Black has a pawn on c5. I need to decide on my next move to continue developing my pieces and controlling the center. A common response to the Sicilian is to play Nc3, developing the knight and controlling d5.

Black has developed their knight to c6, a standard move in the Sicilian Defense. I have a knight on c3 and a pawn on e4. I need to continue developing my pieces. A common move is to play d4, challenging Black's center and opening the diagonal for my light-squared bishop.
